title: A PBM settlement can specify rebate pass-through and pharmacy-access controls while projected savings remain unobserved
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission Caremark Rx and Zinc Health Services settlement announcement and official case materials
geography: United States prescription-drug patients, plan sponsors, and community pharmacies affected by Caremark PBM practices

observations.period: July 14, 2026 Caremark settlement announcement and proposed remedial terms

denominator.unit: FTC Caremark settlement case; public materials do not provide a complete patient, prescription, plan, or pharmacy denominator

projected_consumer_savings.unit: U.S. dollars of consumer savings the FTC says the settlement locks in over up to 10 years

projected_point_of_sale_savings.unit: U.S. dollars of additional patient savings the FTC says may be unlocked over up to 10 years through point-of-sale rebates

remedy_mechanisms.value: delinks PBM fees from drug list prices, offers plan-sponsor designs with rebates passed through at the point of sale, and bars discrimination against lower-list-price versions of covered drugs

pharmacy_and_hub_controls.value: provides community pharmacies an opportunity to shift to cost-plus reimbursement and addresses alleged interference with patient and pharmacy access to hub pharmacy services

consumer_conversion.unit: implemented compliance, prescription-level out-of-pocket cost, fill completion, adherence, medication access, pharmacy revenue, household recovery, or patient trust

observations.method: Structured extraction from the FTC settlement announcement and official case materials. FTC savings projections, mechanism terms, pharmacy/hub provisions, and downstream patient outcomes are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The savings figures are FTC projections over up to 10 years, not observed patient savings. Public materials do not establish implementation, the affected patient or prescription denominator, individual out-of-pocket prices, fill or adherence outcomes, pharmacy participation, or household recovery.
observations.subgroup: Patients exposed to insulin and other prescription-drug list-price and rebate arrangements, plan sponsors, community pharmacies, and users of hub pharmacy services.
observations.counterinterpretation: Pass-through and reimbursement options may improve incentives or transparency without producing equal savings for every patient; plan design, deductible status, formulary choices, pharmacy participation, and implementation can determine who benefits.

related_sources.claim: The FTC case page identifies the Caremark and Zinc Health Services matter and links official case materials.
The FTC PBM topic page identifies the settlement's transparency, point-of-sale, pharmacy, and insulin-price context.

boundary: This record advances a bounded prescription-price and market-power route from PBM rebate and access allegations into specified settlement controls. It does not establish realized savings, lower individual out-of-pocket cost, completed prescriptions, adherence, pharmacy participation, household recovery, or durable trust.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Canonical FTC settlement announcement URL string used as a stable source identifier; official case and topic links are retained for reproduction.
